WHOLESALE FUEL FRAUD

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Wholesale Fuel Retails are under cutting retail competitors and defrauding South Africans – of tax money. Government doing NADA. NOTHING. ZULTZ.

Unique Selling Point:
UNDERCOVER STINGS BUYING FUEL FROM THREE OF THE CULPRITS. CONFRONTS WITH THESE THREE OPERATORS. PUT GOVERNMENT ON THE SPOT FOR IN ACTION.

Further information:
UNDERCOVER STINGS BUYING FUEL FROM THREE OF THE CULPRITS. CONFRONTS WITH THESE THREE OPERATORS. PUT GOVERNMENT ON THE SPOT FOR IN ACTION.

HOW IT WORKS WHEN YOU SELL FUEL:
OPTION 1: RETAIL LICENCE
You are able to sell to the public – this is a garage / petrol station

OPTION 2: WHOLESALE LICENCE
You CAN’T sell to the public – must have a depot and storage facility. Must sell minimum of 1500 liters per TRANSACTION – so not 65l for your car’s tank.

We have a list of at least 17 wholesalers selling to the public – some with licences – some without out. THIS IS ILLEGAL. THEY ARE STEALING FROM SARS, AND ESSENTIALLY SOUTH AFRICANS. SOME OF THESE ARE NOT EVEN REGISTERED OR LICENSED AT ALL!

HOW ARE THEY UNDERCUTTING THE MARKET
RETAIL DIESEL FROM PETROL STATIONS IS R15.04

WHOLESALERS SELLING FOR AS LITTLE AS R13.90 – much cheaper, stealing the market.

WHAT’s GOVERNMENT DOING?
NOTHING. This list has been reported to the Department’s Compliance Department – they have done nothing. Instead they have targeted some of the retailers that complained about the wholesalers selling illegally.

UNDERCOVER - WE DO FOUR PLACES - TWO UNREGISTERED, TWO REGISTERED

INTERVIEWS
- LEGIT RETAILERS
- FUEL LICENCE CONSULTANT – EXPLAINING THE PROCESS
- UNDERCOVER

- DEPARTMENT OF MINERAL RESOUCES AND ENERGY

Script:


FINAL SCRIPT

VO: The fuel industry is a dirty business. It’s big bucks and it’s cut throat.

LINK: Fuel is the central nerve of the economy in an energy hungry country. It’s a huge market that’s increasingly being threatened by illegal operators trying to get their share of the profits – by hook or by crook.

VO: When it comes to trading in fuel there are two types of role players – wholesalers and retailers – each category with its own licence, rules and regulations and hefty price tag for registration and set up costs.

With almost two decades in the industry, Licenced Retailer Jacqueline Meintjes was concerned by a recent dip in her monthly trade.

JACQUELINE: We saw a dramatic decrease in business, clients left us and then we noticed a lot of depots popping up everywhere

VO: Legal retailers were losing up to 35% of their trade by volume, in the area surrounding Meintjes operation. Fuel licencing consultant, Johan Ferreira was called in to investigate this sudden spike in new depots.

He found not everyone is licenced, and not everyone plays by the rules.

JOHAN: there's a lot of sites around them just selling and publicly advertise diesel especially is at very low prices. we're looking at about four to five million litres in a very small area

REGGIE: Retailers are losing business day and night. If we allow this situation of illegal trading coming in it's going to destroy the retailing market

VO: Reggie Sibiya from the Fuel Retailers Association explains that the industry is being impacted severely

REGGIE: This is a volume driven business. The margins for retailing are very thin. if your volumes then drop. You are in a really serious serious problem.

LINK: Diesel pricing is not regulated – this means while there is a base price per litre – you’ll easily find different fuel stations selling at different prices.

JOHAN: These days the room for discount but doing this discount becomes too big. Then it's questionable

VO: The current going rate for retail diesel at your big name fuel stations ranges from about R14.50 to just over R15.

REGGIE: some of these people are selling at the prices at which the retailer gets the product. You cannot do that because from wholesale price you then need to build all your expenses. You know your wages electricity everything else.

VO: Keen to put some of the cheap fuel traders to the test – we rigged a normal unmarked bakkie with hidden cameras and sent in private investigator Armand Trollip.

He went to four sites on Johannesburg's East Rand.

ARMAND: Drove in as you would do at a petrol filling station where you ask for whatever transaction you know 100 150 Rand Diesel. No questions were asked

VO: He paid cash at each operator and was given a receipt every time.

Siyanda Pomona – charged R14,14 per litre
Destiny Diesel Depot – came in R13,90.
While Pomona Diesel & Truck Stop – charged R13,60.
And the cheapest was Fill n Save – at just R13,43.

JAN: The numbers of illegal sites are multiplying too such to such an extent that if something is not done urgently, we faced a total collapse of the of the fuel petroleum industry.

VO: Attorney Jan du Toit represents some of the licenced retailers – he says to be selling at these rates – there are two possible scenarios at play.

JAN: Contravening the Act simply by not not detailing all selling with licenses at all. Alternatively they convene contravening the Act by going outside the parameters of the conditions that is inherent in these licenses.

LINK: It’s easy to be duped into thinking these are legitimate operations – with clear advertising and competitive pricing. But behind the façade – this operation is not registered to sell to the public – it’ trading illegally.

VO: It was time to get some answers from the owner.

MAC: Do you have a licence to retail to the public?
OWNER: A Retail licence?
MAC: ja
OWNER: NO
MAC: Wholesale
OWNER: ya
MAC: private cars are filling up - that’s illegal
OWNER: So what we do is we have accounts. And the guys put deposit

VO: But that’s not what happened when the investigator bought the day before and again just minutes earlier.

Mac:. I don't have and account with you
Owner: that is wrong x3

VO: Deputy Director Tseliso Maqubela, the controller for Petroleum Regulation says the legislation is clear.

MAQUBELA: you are not allowed to operate in both spaces – if you area a wholesaler you can not sell directly to the public

VO: According to the Petroleum Products Act: wholesale means the purchase and sale in bulk - which is defined as 1500 litres or more, per transaction. While the owner blamed his staff for the private sales - he believes he’s found a loophole in the law.

OWNER: you tell me No I want to place order 1500 liters I take a thousand litres and then today you come and you put 200. What do you come up with 300 //The definition of a transaction is in order. It's not payment.
MAC: A transaction is a transaction which means one transaction. But we can fight
OWNER: I’m not fight But what I'm saying is what I'm saying is you're absolutely right.
MAC: So your understanding is wrong.
OWNER: Well no my understanding is different is not wrong.

VO: His understanding is different because it’s wrong, insists Maqubela.

MAQUBELA: he cannot sell 10 times for 150 – it must be one transaction – but to fill in a private vehicle – not allowed

VO: Pomona Diesel & Truck Stop Management were less willing to engage….

MAC: Do you whole sale or do you retail?
LADY: thinks….. retail…
MAC: Can you show me the license.
LADY: I don't have it here the owner’s got.
MAC: OK
LADY: You're supposed to ask permission to come in.
MAC: They let us in at the gate
LADY: I’m calling the police….
MAC: But we're not doing anything wrong.
DOOR CLOSES

VO: The yard manager came out to speak to us.

YARD MANAGER: ………Why would I want to show you?

VO: According to the department - they don’t have a retail licence to show us, only a wholesale licence.

Ferreira says he’s reported a number of transgressors to the authorities, but it doesn’t seem to change anything..

JOHAN: We gave them a list of on about 20 explicitly saying what they are doing what they trespassing

MAQUBELA: I know for a fact that there are three or four where the inspector has gone to the site and issued the relevant notices

JAN: these sites never shut down. None of them adhered to the directives given to them.

VO: One of these sites - is Destiny Diesel Depot. They were quick to whip out a wholesale licence held by Lekholo Holdings and referred us to the owner, Mr Thabang Lekholo.

Despite the large clear signage, the investigator was able to buy diesel on two occasions for a R100 in private vehicles.

MAC CALL: they said that you're the owner. We must speak to you.
THABANG: No no nono

VO: According to Lekolo they are busy finalising a partnership.

THABANG We haven't signed anything anywhere for they don't have a right to tell us how to use my license

MAQUBELA: they are both in violation – they are not allowed to trade using someone else’s licence –

VO: Lekholo referred us to the alleged owner of Destiny Diesel Depot.

MAC: Hi is this MArtin Du Preez
MARTIN: NO
MAC: We got these numbers from Thabang Lekholo and therefore Mr. Martin du Preez from Destiny. Destiny diesel
CALL CUTS

VO: We called back straight away.

UPSOUND: Hi,This is MArtin Du Preez.. I'm not available at the moment. //
MAC: Hauw?! Mr. Martin just said he’s not Mr. Martin du Preez - but his voice message says MArtin Du Preeze.... Okay

VO: Next up we paid Siyanda Fuels a visit. The manager was quick to tell us they had a wholesale licence.

MAC: What does your wholesale licence say to say.
GUY: That I can sell fuel for wholesale
MAC up to 1500 meters right. Yes. We just bought for a hundred rand // which means what you’re doing is illegal.
GUY. he knows very well that they are supposed to only fill fleets.

VO: When the owner arrived, he also resorted to blaming the staff.

ENVER: Yesterday a day before we won't allow any. Of you to come in. We did WARN the attendants

MAC: But the attendants are not to charge you. You guys are the owners
ENVER: We are not here all the time.
MAC: if you've got a slip book for these kind of things it means you're allowing it to happen
ENVER: Let me investigate it.
MAC: You're taking the money.
ENVER: they're not supposed to supposed to
MAC: We know they’re not supposed to otherwise we wouldn’t be here

VO: Realising we’ve caught them overstepping the rules – the owner turned on us.

ENVER: Can you do me a favour please can you. Can you put your camera off…
WHACKS CAMERA

VO: They then refused to open the gates and in an ironic twist claimed they were calling the cops on us, even though they had broken the law.

Maqubela admits these illegal operations are an indictment on his department.

MAQUBELA: the buck stops with me – we will make sure all those sights have been vested – and action has taken we need to stop those operations with immediate effect - be tougher on how we implement this.

LINK: If you’re caught operating without a licence or contravening licence conditions you could be whacked with a fine not exceeding R1 million or 10 years in prison – but very few if any culprits have faced these consequences.

REGGIE: Nothing is being done that that the reason that this thing is like on a rampart is because people are seeing the opportunity. They don't see any action. people realize that you know you've got a watchdog with no with no teeth

JAN: That department has completely failed in their obligation. They proceed by by legislation. There's absolutely no fear for the department by these people that are emboldened multiplying significantly.

VO: While Maqubela agrees More should be done - their resources are limited with only one inspector per province - increased human capacity will be necessary.

MAQUBELA: we cannot win the war if we don’t work with local government //We need to look at stopping operations – it is only when you stop the money this thing will stop.





PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: The fuel industry is a dirty business. We go undercover into South Africa’s lucrative fuel sales market --- where some retailers are trading illegally – undercutting competitors and flouting the law.

PROMO 2
VO: An investigation into South Africa’s lucrative fuel sales market --- where operators are illegally selling cheap fuel and undercutting competitors We expose some of the culprits.

PROMO 3
VO: The Fuel industry is being plagued by illegal operators – undercutting legitimate traders in an already cut throat industry. Our investigation exposes some of the transgressors.
